2. **Sensitivity of the test (P(Pos | Disease))**: 92% or 0.92 (the probability of testing positive given that the person has the disease)
3. **Specificity of the test (P(Neg | No Disease))**: 88% or 0.88 (the probability of testing negative given that the person does not have the disease)

From the specificity, we can derive the probability of a false positive:
- **P(Pos | No Disease)**: 1 - Specificity = 1 - 0.88 = 0.12 (the probability of testing positive when the person does not have the disease)

The probability that a person has the disease given that they tested positive (P(Disease | Pos)) can be calculated as follows:

\[
P(Disease | Pos) = \frac{P(Pos | Disease) \cdot P(Disease)}{P(Pos)}
\]

Where \( P(Pos) \) can be calculated using the law of total probability:

\[
P(Pos) = P(Pos | Disease) \cdot P(Disease) + P(Pos | No Disease) \cdot P(No Disease)
\]

5. **Calculating \( P(No Disease) \)**:
\[
P(No Disease) = 1 - P(Disease) = 1 - 0.03 = 0.97
